## Conclusion


Given the analysis we performed, our data supports the idea that LS questions aid with understaning of course material. Our histogram portrays that the majority of students rated LS questions as effective. Further, our catplot demonstrates a positive correlation between LS questions effectiveness and understanding, with an effectiveness rating of 6 being associated with the greatest understanding rating. While some of our analysis shows that low LS effectiveness is also associated with high understanding, this may occur since some students have previous programming expereince, and therefore have a high understanding of the material without finding the LS questions effective. Given our analysis, we recommend that the the course includes a greater number of LS question assignments because they improve understanding of material, which may in turn improve overall grades for students. One refinement to this idea is that there should be more LS assignments depending on the topic. For example, harder topics like recursion could have a greater number of LS question assignments. A cost of this idea is that the instructional team will have to spend more time creating these assignments. Further, it is a larger number of assignemnts for the instructional team to grade. Despite this, the overall student beenfit of greater understanding of course material outweights the costs.
